$note: DS-33 shared design tokens. Values are transcribed from the live LIT player CSS/TS, which is the single source of truth (PRD.md §4A is the secondary description). Every group carries a top-level `source` listing the files it was read from; every token also carries its own `source` selector for traceability. Colors are stored as {hex, alpha} pairs so build.mjs can emit both `rgba()` (CSS) and `Color(hex:opacity:)` (Swift) from one number. A leaf may carry `cssOnly: "<reason>"` when its value is a CSS-only mechanism (a `calc()`/`env()`/`polygon()`/grid-template string) with no portable SwiftUI form; build.mjs and tokens.test.ts both honor that flag instead of silently dropping anything.

sourceFiles: src/player3d/player-app.ts (LCD_FLASH_MS constant only, referenced by lcd-text.ts's buttonFlash)
src/style.css (Vite template leftover; read only to flag the stray global button rule, see disagreementsWithPrdTable)
meta.criticRound2Note: Round 1 missed that src/player3d/hud.ts adds the class `p3d-mono` to many elements in JS (readout values, panel meta, track num/dur, repeat button, sheet toggle, insert button, open hint, access links, error text/action, strip, boot) whose own CSS rule does not itself declare font-family. Reading hud.ts + hud-fx.ts in full for round 2 corrected several type roles from Inter to JetBrains Mono (see type.* below) and added the hud-fx oscilloscope/sparkline colors, boot terminal content/cadence, and the exact DOM class list.
disagreementsWithPrdTable: Destructive red (DS-2 color table left it as 'take the exact value from ios.css'): found #FF5F6D at .account-actions .text-btn in src/ios.css.

DS-29 states one blanket press-scale of 0.97. Code has three different values: 0.97 (body.ios-app .product-card:active, matches DS-29), 0.985 (body.ios-app .action-card:active, lighter squish), 0.92 (.ios-tab:active, heavier squish). Recorded all three under motion.pressScale.*.

DS-21 states a blanket '2 pt gold outline on focus'. The primary button's own focus ring (.p3d-insert:focus-visible) is actually a WHITE 3px outline with 4px offset, not gold 2px. It is also NOT a single blanket offset elsewhere: the default is gold/2px/+2 (.p3d-key, .p3d-volume__input, .p3d-repeat, .p3d-sheet-toggle), but .p3d-track:focus-visible is INSET (-2px offset, gold/2px) and .nav-peek / .mini-player__bar are +3px offset (still gold/2px). Recorded as shape.focusRing (the +2 default) plus component.listRow.focusRingOffsetPt (-2) and component.peripheralFocusRingOffsetPt (+3), and component.primaryButton.focusRing (white/3px/+4).

DS-27 describes one 'gold corner tick motif' shared everywhere. Code actually has three distinct weights, and TWO OF THEM ARE NOT GOLD: the HUD panel tick is full gold, 14x14px, 2px border, both top-left and bottom-right corners (hud.css .p3d-panel::before/::after, border-color: var(--gold)). The site card tick (theme.css .product-card::before etc.) and the mini-player tick (theme.css .mini-player::before) are both `--line` (gold at 60% alpha), not `--gold`, 1px border, ONE corner only (top-left). Corrected component.nowPlaying.cornerTick.color and the new component.siteCard.cornerTick.color to "line", not "gold".

DS-21 states a blanket 'minimum 44 pt targets'. Several existing controls fall under 44px: .p3d-access__link (40px), .mini-player__key (34px desktop / 40px phone), .mini-player__close (26px), .ios-nav__slot .cart-btn (34x34px, ios.css:164-166), .download-btn/.download-card .primary-btn (min-height 34px, ios.css:326-329), .nav-peek (56x26px, hud.css:1192-1193). These are pre-existing and were not changed (out of this piece's file boundary); flagged for the lead/critic.

DS-29 describes scene reveals fading 'over about 3 s'. The literal CSS is two separate rules sharing the same value: hud.css:1290-1294 (.p3d-hud, .p3d-insert, .p3d-inspect-hint { transition: opacity 2.6s ease 0.6s }) and hud.css:1162-1164 (.stream-page .main-nav { transition: opacity 2.6s ease 0.6s }) — a 2.6s opacity transition with a 0.6s delay, i.e. ~3.2s from trigger to fully revealed, not a flat 3s.

theme.css declares a second 'opaque panel' representation, `--panel-solid: #0B0A12` (alpha 1), distinct from the alpha-0.95 rgba(9,8,16,0.95) that hud.css actually swaps `--panel` to on tablet/sheet surfaces (DS-19's '0.95 on opaque sheets'). `--panel-solid` does not appear to be consumed anywhere else in the CSS read for this piece. Both are recorded (color.panel, color.panelSheet, color.panelSolid).

DS-13's chamfer-cut panel geometry belongs to the 3D HUD (.p3d-panel) only. The rest of the site (theme.css product/account/stats cards, buttons) uses ordinary border-radius (2px buttons, 4px cards) and ios.css grouped lists use 14px radius / 999px pills — none of it uses the chamfer/tick motif. Both systems are recorded as they exist; unifying them site-wide is explicitly a later step per this task's instructions, not part of DS-33.

DS-10 (primary button, 'Inter 800'): the live DOM adds `p3d-mono` to the insert button (hud.ts: `el('button', 'p3d-insert p3d-mono', 'INSERT DISC')`), and .p3d-insert's own CSS does not set font-family, so `p3d-mono`'s JetBrains Mono wins — it renders in mono, not Inter. Only mono weights 500/600/700 are loaded, so the declared font-weight:800 has no matching face; the browser renders the heaviest available real face (700/Bold), and may synthesize extra weight on top depending on the engine. Corrected type.primaryButton.family to jetbrainsMono and recorded the rendered weight.

DS-17 (readouts): .p3d-readout__value, .p3d-track__num/.p3d-track__dur, and .p3d-panel__meta are all built in hud.ts with the `p3d-mono` class (readout() helper, setTracks(), and the two `p3d-panel__meta p3d-mono` header spans), not Inter as round 1 assumed. None of these set an explicit font-weight in CSS, so the default 400 has no matching mono face (500/600/700 loaded) and the browser renders the nearest heavier match: Medium (500). Corrected type.readoutValue, type.trackNumDur, type.panelMeta to family jetbrainsMono with the rendered weight noted. (.p3d-repeat and .p3d-sheet-toggle are also built with `p3d-mono` in hud.ts, but both declare font-weight:700 explicitly, an exact match for a loaded face, so they render as declared — corrected their `family` to jetbrainsMono for accuracy, but there is no weight-substitution issue there.)

DS-29's 0.6s overlay fade is the boot loader's own fade-out only (.p3d-boot, hud.css ~503). A SEPARATE, undocumented-in-the-PRD 0.42s opacity fade (plus a 10px translate) governs the primary button / inspect hint / open hint appearing and disappearing mid-session (hud.css:1384-1391, .p3d-insert/.p3d-inspect-hint/.p3d-open-hint). Recorded as motion.midSessionOverlayFadeS = 0.42, distinct from motion.overlayFadeS = 0.6.

DS-18 says grouped lists (settings, account, lend details) are each 'a HUDPanel'. The live ios.css grouped lists (.dashboard-actions, .account-card, .orders-list, .download-card) do NOT use the HUDPanel chamfer/corner-tick treatment at all: they are plain rgba(245,241,230,0.05)-fill rounded rectangles (14px radius, 1px lineDim border) with simple 1px cream separators (rgba(245,241,230,0.1)) inset to the text (57px for action rows, 14px for order rows) — a different, simpler visual system than a HUDPanel. Recorded as the new component.groupedList group, and flagged as a real gap between the PRD's description and the shipped CSS.

DS-15 (secondary/key button) implies the sharp, un-rounded HUD aesthetic, and .p3d-key correctly has no border-radius of its own. But src/style.css (the un-cleaned Vite scaffold stylesheet, still loaded on every page) carries a bare-element `button { border-radius: 8px; ... }` rule (src/style.css:85-95) that WOULD apply an 8px radius to any real `<button>` not covered by a more specific class selector. Because `.p3d-key` etc. are class selectors they win the specificity fight and stay sharp-cornered in practice, but this is a latent, unintended default sitting under the whole site, not a DS-15 value — recorded under shape.strayGlobalButtonRadiusPt with an explicit 'do not adopt' note.

The same src/style.css rule set also carries `button:hover { border-color: #646cff; }` (src/style.css:97-99) — the Vite scaffold's default indigo hover, a direct DS-3 violation ('no default blue tint anywhere') on any un-classed button. Recorded under color.strayGlobalButtonHover and flagged: this must never be copied into the app; it is scaffold debt to clean up on the site, not a design token.

pulseCycleS.swiftNote: CSS `animation: p3d-pulse 1.8s ease-in-out infinite` runs ONE 1.8s cycle per iteration (a single keyframe pass, 0%->50%->100%). SwiftUI's `.repeatForever(autoreverses: true)` instead runs the given duration forward THEN backward each cycle, so to land on the same 1.8s total, `Animation.easeInOut(duration: 0.9).repeatForever(autoreverses: true)` must be used (0.9 forward + 0.9 back = 1.8s), not duration: 1.8.
pulseCycleS.source: DS-14; hud.css @keyframes p3d-pulse, animation: p3d-pulse 1.8s ease-in-out infinite

eqAnim.source: hud.css @keyframes p3d-eq (now-playing tracklist EQ bars) — full keyframe values under component.listRow.eq.keyframes

terminalTypingMinMs.source: hud-fx.ts BootTerminal.type(): window.setTimeout(tick, 14 + Math.random() * 12) — lower bound, 2 chars revealed per tick

askPulseS.swiftNote: same single-midpoint (50%) keyframe shape as pulseCycleS — SwiftUI repeatForever(autoreverses:true) needs half the CSS duration to match the real 1.8s total.

openPulseS.swiftNote: same single-midpoint (50%) keyframe shape as pulseCycleS — SwiftUI repeatForever(autoreverses:true) needs half the CSS duration to match the real 2.6s total.

navPeekBobS.swiftNote: an asymmetric 4-stage keyframe (0%/68%/80%/100%, not a symmetric midpoint), not representable as a simple SwiftUI Animation curve — drive it with a discrete keyframe/phase animation (e.g. PhaseAnimator) using this duration, not Animation.easeInOut.repeatForever.

radialGaugeEaseMs.source: hud-fx.ts RadialGauge.set(): const t = Math.min(1, (now - this.startedAt) / 600); easeOut = (t) => 1 - Math.pow(1 - t, 3)

layout.note: All ratios are relative to the LCD canvas's own W (width) or H (height), matching lcd.ts draw(): padX=W*0.055, advance=(W-2*padX)/11, cw=advance*0.74, ch=cw/0.56, t(segment thickness)=cw*0.15, g(segment gap)=t*0.32, inset=H*0.07, bezel corner radius=H*0.06, baseline=H-inset-H*0.14, glow shadowBlur=H*0.045, diagonal segment normal offset=t*0.42, diagonal 'd' placement offset=t*0.72, flag size=min(H*0.16, top-inset-H*0.08), flag y=inset+H*0.08, flag spacing=flagSize*1.9 per index.

pause.note: two rects, each width=size*0.3 height=size, second offset x by size*0.55

repeat.note: outer=size/2, inner=outer*0.62 (=size*0.31), ring arc from -0.35π to 1.35π rad (-63deg to 243deg), plus a small arrowhead polygon at the ring's start

flags.source: player3d/lcd.ts draw() flags array and repeatIcon()

statusFormat.rule: Any raw content.text is LEFT-justified and space-padded to characterCount (11) by lcd.ts draw(): `text.toUpperCase().padEnd(11).slice(0,11)`. The playing/paused/stopped/resuming statuses and the next/prev button flashes are instead built by lcd-text.ts's `lcdLine(left, right)`, which RIGHT-justifies `right` (the 2-digit track number) against the end of the 11-char field: `room = 11 - right.length; (left.slice(0, room).padEnd(room) + right).slice(0, 11)`.
statusFormat.source: player3d/lcd-text.ts lcdLine(), STATUS_LINE, buttonFlash(); player3d/lcd.ts draw()

glyphs.segmentBitsNote: Bit index N means `1 << N`. Outer ring: a(top) b c(right, top-to-bottom) d(bottom) e f(left, bottom-to-top). Middle bar: g1(left half) g2(right half). Inner strokes from centre: h(to top-left) i(up) j(to top-right) k(to bottom-left) l(down) m(to bottom-right).

table.0: a b c d e f
table.2: a b d e g1 g2
table.5: a c d f g1 g2
table.6: a c d e f g1 g2
table.8: a b c d e f g1 g2
table.9: a b c d f g1 g2
table.A: a b c e f g1 g2
table.B: a b c d g2 i l
table.D: a b c d i l
table.G: a c d e f g2
table.H: b c e f g1 g2
table.M: b c e f h j
table.N: b c e f h m
table.O: a b c d e f
table.P: a b e f g1 g2
table.Q: a b c d e f m
table.R: a b e f g1 g2 m
table.S: a c d f g1 g2
table.W: b c e f k m

glyphs.tableNote: Each value is a space-separated list of lit segment names (matching player3d/lcd-text.ts GLYPHS exactly, character-for-character). build.mjs computes the Swift bitmask (`1 << segmentBits[name]` OR'd together) for each entry so the source of truth stays the readable segment-letter form, not a hand-computed integer.

widthExpr.cssOnly: CSS min()/vw; on iOS use `min(280, screenWidth * 0.7)`
CSS min()/vw; on iOS use `min(360, screenWidth * 0.8)`

terminal.source: hud.ts new BootTerminal([...lines], reducedMotion); hud-fx.ts BootTerminal.type()
